result.summary:
Rework iteration 1 of 3 on docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md, addressing the single FAIL finding in handoffs/WF02-REQ-026/step-03b-test-design-validator.json: AC8's assertion mechanics were confirmed sound, but the spec falsely claimed (in the AC8 section, the Independence note's AC8 bullet, and the Coverage table's AC8 row) that this spec's 'neither non-doors item's own time leaks' assertion closes a coverage gap in BACKEND-DEV's committed reminderJobs.db.test.ts AC8 case.

Verified the finding myself before rewriting: read apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.db.test.ts lines 440-489 directly. The committed `it('AC8: ...')` block already contains, at lines 479-487, exactly the assertion this spec claimed was missing -- `if (networkingText !== startsText) { expect(message.caption).not.toContain(networkingText); }` and the identical guard for closingText. My original citation ('lines ~477 onward... asserts .not.toContain(doorsLabel) only') stopped reading at line 477 and missed the immediately-following lines in the same test body. The false claim is corrected in all three cited spots; the AC8 case itself is kept (not removed), re-grounded solely on its legitimate, independently-verified value: the deliberately different agenda-`kind` vocabulary (`"workshop"`/`"afterparty"` here vs BACKEND-DEV's `"networking"`/`"close"`), which genuinely tests that findDoorsAgendaItem's `kind === "doors"` check is a real string-equality test against the literal value, not something that happens to also reject BACKEND-DEV's own two chosen strings for some other structural reason (e.g. a length check or a hardcoded blocklist).

Three corrections made in docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md:

1. Independence note's AC8 bullet (originally lines 29-32): appended a clause stating plainly that BACKEND-DEV's own committed AC8 case already asserts the 'neither non-doors item's own time leaks' property (citing the real lines, 479-487) and that this case does not close a gap there -- the vocabulary swap is stated as this case's sole independent value.

2. AC8 section's 3rd pass condition and failure-mode paragraph (originally lines 358-377): removed the false 'closes that gap' sentence and the false 'not directly asserted by name in BACKEND-DEV's own AC8 case' claim (both citing only line ~477). Replaced with an accurate statement that BACKEND-DEV's case already contains this exact assertion at lines 479-487, and re-stated the case's value as the kind-vocabulary difference. Rewrote the failure-mode paragraph to match: the case now catches a `findDoorsAgendaItem` bug that matches on something other than a genuine `kind === "doors"` equality (e.g. a hardcoded blocklist of BACKEND-DEV's specific strings, or a length/position/count-based check) -- such a bug would still pass BACKEND-DEV's own AC8 case (whose specific non-doors strings it happens to reject) but would fail this case's different vocabulary, exposing that the underlying check was never a genuine equality test.

3. Coverage table's AC8 row: replaced 'asserts absence of doors label AND both non-doors items' own times' (which implied that assertion was this case's novel contribution) with wording that states the case re-runs the same assertion shape BACKEND-DEV's case already has, using a different agenda-`kind` vocabulary, and that its actual, independent value is confirming `kind === "doors"` is a real equality check rather than vocabulary-specific.

No other AC, the shared setup, AC7's own section, AC9, AC10, the forged-callback section, or any other part of the spec was touched -- this is confined to the three spots the validator's finding named, per the task's explicit instruction. The AC8 test case's actual code/fixture (agenda kind strings, assertions, pass conditions themselves) is unchanged -- only its stated justification/framing was corrected.
